newsitem.title: LITHUANIA: FINANCE MINISTRY WELCOMES S&P RATING.
newsitem.headline: FINANCE MINISTRY WELCOMES S&P RATING.

text.p: Lithuanian Finance Minister Algirdas Shemeta welcomed the soverign invesment grade rating assigned to his country by Standard and Poor's (S&P) on Monday, describing it as a big success.
Standard and Poor's said earlier that it had assigned Lithuania a BBB minus rating for its long-term foreign currency debt and a BBB plus rating for its long-term local currency debt.
It also assigned Lithuania an A-3 rating for its short-term foriegn currency and an A-2 for its short-term local currency.
"For the first time Lithuania was given an investment grade credit rating...and it was two notches higher than our first rating from Moody's last September," Shemeta told a news conference.
Moody's last September assigned Lithuania a sovereign ceiling of Ba2 for its foreign currency bonds and notes.
"This is a big success," he said.
He also said that the higher rating reflected the government's commitment to increasing the pace of market reforms and privatising key companies.
He added that S&P was impressed with the sharp fall in inflation and the country's low burden of external and internal debt.
The rating is regarded as crucial to the success of Lithuania's upcoming eurobond issue.
